/-!
# Conjecture 3.16

by M. I. Kargapolov

The word problem for a group admitting a single defining relation in the variety
of soluble groups of derived length $n$, $n \geq 3$.

Let $\mathfrak{A}^n$ be the variety of soluble groups of derived length (at most) $n$, i.e.
the groups $G$ with $G^{(n)} = 1$, and let $F_m$ be the free group of finite rank $m$. A group
with a single defining relation $r \in F_m$ in the variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ is the group
$$G = F_m / \bigl(F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle\bigr),$$
where $F_m^{(n)}$ is the $n$-th term of the derived series of $F_m$; equivalently, $G$ is
the quotient of the free soluble group $F_m / F_m^{(n)}$ of derived length $n$ by the normal
closure of the image of $r$. The word problem for $G$ asks for an algorithm deciding, for a
word $w$ in the letters $x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}$, whether $w = 1$ in $G$.

The problem asks whether the word problem is decidable for every such group when $n \geq 3$.
For $n = 1$ and $n = 2$ the word problem for such groups is known to be decidable.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

The normal subgroup $F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$ of the free group
$F_m$ of rank `m` generated by the $n$-th derived subgroup $F_m^{(n)}$ together with the
relator `r`. Since both factors are normal, their product is their join.

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → ∀ (m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)),
      ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin m × Bool) =>
        (FreeGroup.mk w : OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r) = 1 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Is the word problem decidable for every group with a single defining relation in the variety
of soluble groups of derived length $n$, for every $n \geq 3$?

For the group $G = F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$, the word problem
is the predicate on words $w$ over the alphabet $\{x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}\}$
(elements of `List (Fin m × Bool)`, read in $F_m$ via `FreeGroup.mk`) that holds exactly when
$w$ represents the identity of $G$. The word problem for a fixed group $G$ is decidable when
this predicate is computable.

claims.decomposer_note: Terse entry naming a yes/no decidability question: is the word problem decidable for every group with one defining relation in the variety A^n (finite rank m, relator r, i.e. F_m / (F_m^{(n)} · ⟨⟨r⟩⟩)), with implicit universal quantifiers over n ≥ 3, the finite rank m and the relator r; 'derived length n' means the variety A^n (derived length ≤ n), 'decidable' needs a computability notion such as ComputablePred on words of FreeGroup (Fin m) (n = 1, 2 are known decidable, n ≥ 3 open, no remarks/star so not solved).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates encode the same proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 3, ∀ finite rank m, ∀ relator r ∈ F_m, ComputablePred on words List (Fin m × Bool) of 'FreeGroup.mk w is trivial in F_m/(F_m^{(n)}·⟨⟨r⟩⟩)'. I verified in Mathlib that derivedSeries G n is G^{(n)} (derivedSeries G 0 = ⊤), so `3 ≤ n` is exactly n ≥ 3 and the kernel derivedSeries F n ⊔ normalClosure {r} is the product of the two normal subgroups defining the one-relator group in the variety A^n; FreeGroup.mk is the surjective word→element map with of i = mk [(i,true)], (of i)⁻¹ = mk [(i,false)]; ComputablePred is genuine (Nat.Partrec-based) computability, and the Primcodable instance on List (Fin m × Bool) resolves. Quantifiers all sit after answer(sorry); answer(True) = decidable for every such group, answer(False) = some such group has undecidable word problem; the RHS is non-trivial so the answer is constrained. Boundary cases m = 0 and r = 1 give trivially/known-decidable groups and do not alter the universal claim. c07 was chosen because its named quotient `OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r` makes the statement read literally as 'w = 1 in G', and it ships compiling `category test` lemmas checking r = 1 in G and derivedSeries G n = ⊥ (i.e. G ∈ A^n), which the repo encourages for bespoke definitions. I checked that c07's predicate is provably equivalent (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff) to the membership form used by c01–c03, c06, c08. Only docstring edits were made; the file compiles with just the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.16

by M. I. Kargapolov

The word problem for a group admitting a single defining relation in the variety
of soluble groups of derived length $n$, $n \geq 3$.

Let $\mathfrak{A}^n$ be the variety of soluble groups of derived length (at most) $n$, i.e.
the groups $G$ with $G^{(n)} = 1$, and let $F_m$ be the free group of finite rank $m$. A group
with a single defining relation $r \in F_m$ in the variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ is the group
$$G = F_m / \bigl(F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle\bigr),$$
where $F_m^{(n)}$ is the $n$-th term of the derived series of $F_m$; equivalently, $G$ is
the quotient of the free soluble group $F_m / F_m^{(n)}$ of derived length $n$ by the normal
closure of the image of $r$. The word problem for $G$ asks for an algorithm deciding, for a
word $w$ in the letters $x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}$, whether $w = 1$ in $G$.

The problem asks whether the word problem is decidable for every such group when $n \geq 3$.
For $n = 1$ and $n = 2$ the word problem for such groups is known to be decidable.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.16»

open Subgroup

variable (m n : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m))

/-- The normal subgroup $F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$ of the free group
$F_m$ of rank `m` generated by the $n$-th derived subgroup $F_m^{(n)}$ together with the
relator `r`. Since both factors are normal, their product is their join. -/
def relators : Subgroup (FreeGroup (Fin m)) :=
  derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n ⊔ normalClosure {r}

instance : (relators m n r).Normal :=
  haveI := derivedSeries_normal (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n
  sup_normal _ _

/-- The group with generators $x_1, \dots, x_m$ and the single defining relation $r = 1$ in the
variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ of soluble groups of derived length $n$, that is,
$F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$. -/
abbrev OneRelatorSolubleGroup : Type :=
  FreeGroup (Fin m) ⧸ relators m n r

/--
Is the word problem decidable for every group with a single defining relation in the variety
of soluble groups of derived length $n$, for every $n \geq 3$?

For the group $G = F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$, the word problem
is the predicate on words $w$ over the alphabet $\{x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}\}$
(elements of `List (Fin m × Bool)`, read in $F_m$ via `FreeGroup.mk`) that holds exactly when
$w$ represents the identity of $G$. The word problem for a fixed group $G$ is decidable when
this predicate is computable.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → ∀ (m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)),
      ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin m × Bool) =>
        (FreeGroup.mk w : OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r) = 1 := by
  sorry

/-- The relator `r` is trivial in `OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem coe_relator_eq_one : (r : OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r) = 1 :=
  (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff r).2 <| mem_sup_right <| subset_normalClosure rfl

/-- `OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r` is soluble of derived length at most `n`, i.e. it lies in
the variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem derivedSeries_eq_bot : derivedSeries (OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r) n = ⊥ := by
  rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (relators m n r)) n,
    Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff, QuotientGroup.ker_mk']
  exact le_sup_left

end Kourovka.«3.16»

items: "Group admitting a single defining relation in the variety of soluble groups of derived length n" is read as F_m / (F_m^{(n)} · ⟨⟨r⟩⟩) for finite rank m and relator r ∈ F_m (equivalently the free soluble group F_m/F_m^{(n)} of derived length n modulo one relator), following the decomposition table; 'derived length n' is the variety A^n, i.e. derived length ≤ n.

The terse entry is read as the yes/no question "is the word problem decidable for all such groups?", with universal quantifiers over n ≥ 3, m and r placed after `answer(sorry)`. Consequently `answer(True)` = decidable for every n ≥ 3, every m, every r; `answer(False)` = some such group has undecidable word problem. A reading that asks separately for each n (e.g. as a set of n) was not used.

The word problem is the non-uniform one (for each fixed group G = G(m,n,r), the predicate on words is computable), which is the standard meaning of 'the word problem for a group'; the uniform version (algorithm taking r as input) is not what is stated.

Words are elements of `List (Fin m × Bool)` interpreted in the free group via `FreeGroup.mk`; the predicate is `QuotientGroup.mk (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1` in the quotient group. `ComputablePred` existentially quantifies its `DecidablePred`, so no classical instance is needed.

The rank m ranges over all naturals (m = 0 gives the trivial group, harmlessly decidable) and the relator r over all of F_m (r = 1 gives the free soluble group, known decidable); neither degenerate case affects the truth of the biconditional.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities in the source: (1) the entry is terse and names a problem rather than posing a question; following the decomposition table it is read as the yes/no question 'is the word problem decidable for every group with one defining relation in A^n, for every n ≥ 3?' with universal quantifiers over n ≥ 3, m, r. A per-n reading (answer as a set of n) would carry more information if decidability turned out to depend on n, but the collective yes/no reading is the natural formalization of the notebook entry and is what the table fixes. (2) 'derived length n' is read as the variety A^n (derived length ≤ n), the standard meaning of a variety of soluble groups; the test lemma derivedSeries_eq_bot confirms the group lies in A^n. (3) 'Word problem for a group' is the non-uniform one (an algorithm per fixed group), the classical meaning; a uniform-in-(m,r) version would be a stronger different statement. (4) Finite rank m is assumed, as the word problem is only meaningful for finitely generated (or recursively presented) groups; the notes fix this. No candidate omitted the slot; all reports concur on these modeling choices. AMS tags 3 (logic/computability) and 20 (group theory) as in c02/c04/c07, following BranchingVAS.lean's use of tag 3 for decidability questions. The docstring remark that the n = 1, 2 cases are known decidable (abelian; f.g. metabelian groups are residually finite and finitely presented in A^2) is standard background, not part of the formal statement.
statement: The word problem for a group admitting a single defining relation in the variety of soluble groups of derived length $n$, $n \geq 3$.
